source: Department of Finance, Annual Report of the New York City Real Property Tax, Fiscal Year 2026 (July 2026), Fast Facts p. 1 and Tables 1, 4, 19, 20, 21 and 22
period: Fiscal 2026 (July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026), one year only
basis: The levy, the tax billed, by class, as the Department of Finance reports it. A one-year snapshot of billed tax, not the selected year's revenue.
coverage: All four tax classes: the whole fiscal 2026 levy of $37,976.6 million. Not the same total as the first chart's property tax line, which is revenue after refunds and reserves.

classes.label: Class 1, mostly 1-, 2- and 3-family homes
classes.note: Class 1 is mostly one-, two- and three-family homes; it also holds some small condominiums and vacant residential land.

classes.label: Rental apartment buildings
classes.note: Large rental buildings, rental condominium buildings and 4-to-10-family rentals, grouped from the Department of Finance's Table 4. Landlords get the bill; how much of it reaches tenants through rent is not settled.

classes.label: Co-ops, condos and condops
classes.note: State law values co-ops and condos as if they were rentals, so their official market value sits far below sale prices. No effective rate is shown for that reason.

quotes.rptl581: Unless specifically excluded, Section 581 of the Real Property Tax Law prohibits the use of sales data that reflect actual or potential cooperative or condominium ownership in the assessment of multiple-family housing.
quotes.passthrough: Unfortunately, the testimony did not reveal conclusive evidence regarding the degree of the property tax borne by renters. (NYC Advisory Commission on Property Tax Reform, final report, Dec 2021, p.8)

years_note: Each fiscal year's levy by class from the Department of Finance's class-levy history table (the newest annual report that prints the year). Class 2 is divided between rental buildings and co-ops and condos by that year's own reconciliation by property type, gross levy, from fiscal 2005; earlier reports have no levy by property type, so fiscal 2000 to 2004 show Class 2 whole. Before fiscal 2010 condo buildings with rental units are counted with condos.
